messages:
maya: Heads up — noticed a spike in SSE reconnects last night tied to routing fallbacks. Clients get an error event, then enter a tight reconnect loop.

maya: Short log snippet:```
[2026-03-01T12:34:56Z] stream: client connected session=abc123
[2026-03-01T12:34:56Z] runtime: route -> model-a-8q
[2026-03-01T12:34:57Z] runtime: kvcache MISS for prefix len=512
[2026-03-01T12:34:57Z] runtime: fallback -> model-a-4q (capacity tier)
[2026-03-01T12:34:57Z] upstream: 503 ServiceUnavailable
[2026-03-01T12:34:57Z] stream: heartbeat missed, closing stream
```

jordan: Oh interesting — is the heartbeat detection server-side only or also influenced by the client keepalive?

maya: Server-side. Our trace shows we call close_stream(reason=heartbeat_timeout) immediately after the 503, which triggers client reconnect. Client then reopens and sometimes gets routed to the same fallback and loops.

ranjit: That smells like routing not being sticky for mid-stream fallback. If session routing isn't sticky, a reconnect can go to a different pool that also lacks warm KV caches and then fall back again.

lina: Telemetry confirms: dashboard "streaming/reconnects" has a correlated spike at 02:34 UTC and almost all had reason="heartbeat" and route_change=true. Canary rollout 2026-02-28 23:50 made routing policy default to prefer cost-tier fallback, which aligns timewise.

kevin: Repro steps? I can try locally. maya — can you paste the exact curl you used?

maya: Repro with this client (headless):```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?session_id=repro-777&model=model-a&stream=1\"
# then simulate backend capacity by returning 503 on the first chunk
```

jordan: Quick thought: we treat 503 from upstream as fatal now. Maybe we should treat 503 during fallback routing as a transient and attempt an automatic short backoff + retry on the same session/pinned routing instead of closing stream with heartbeat.

ranjit: Agreed — two proposals: 1) keep stream open and buffer a small retry window (e.g., 500ms) for fallback selection to settle; 2) make routing sticky by session_id for N minutes after stream creation so reconnects prefer the same pool while KV warms. Both are config changes, low-risk.

lina: From telemetry POV: add a metric for "fallback-triggered-reconnects" (labelled by session_id, route_from, route_to). Also create a dashboard panel showing reconcile of kvcache hit-rate vs reconnect-rate.

ops-bot: deploy started by deploy-bot on branch fix/sse-fallback-backoff at 2026-03-02T01:12:00Z

kevin: I sketched a minimal server-side patch: on upstream 5xx during in-progress stream, don't call close_stream immediately; mark stream state=degraded and enqueue a single quick retry to a different compatible variant, with exponential backoff up to 2s, then only close if all tries fail. Pseudo:```python
if upstream.status >= 500 and stream.in_progress:
    stream.mark('degraded')
    for try in range(3):
        sleep(0.25 * 2**try)
        if route_to_alternate(stream):
            return continue_stream()
    close_stream(reason='upstream_fail')
```
This avoids heartbeats being interpreted as client-side death and stops tight reconnect storms.

maya: That looks good. Also add a short server-sent comment event so clients see a human-readable transient error instead of immediate EOF. e.g., `: comment retrying on fallback (attempt 2)` so devs see what happened.

jordan: Can we also change the default heartbeat timeout from 10s to 30s for sessions that have just switched routing? Makes sense to give kv warming time. Might increase connection churn cost slightly but prevents rapid reconnects.

ranjit: If we do sticky routing and backoff retry, we can keep heartbeat low for normal fast-path but increase it only when fallback_count>0. Config knobs: `heartbeat.default=10s`, `heartbeat.post_fallback=30s`, `routing.sticky_ttl=300s`.

lina: I'll add the telemetry items and a short alert: if reconnect_rate > 100/min AND > 70% have reason=heartbeat, page oncall. For now set severity=P2.

kevin: Action items: create bug in JIRA, add unit tests for fallback retry logic, add e2e repro harness. I'll open PR for server patch (small change) and a follow-up for routing sticky TTL.

maya: Thanks — assigning the thread to kevin. I attached a small HAR-like dump in the ticket.

jordan: Also document client best-practices: clients should implement jittered exponential reconnect and respect `:comment` SSE messages. Add small snippet in devex docs. Example:```js
// client reconnect pseudocode
let retry = 100;
function onclose(){
  setTimeout(() => open(), retry + Math.random()*50);
  retry = Math.min(retry*2, 5000);
}
```

ranjit: I'll follow up with a perf test to measure cost impact of sticky routing.

lina: Updated dashboard and created metric `stream.fallback_reconnects` (count) and graph panel in #observability.

ops-bot: deploy finished: deploy-bot finished deploy fix/sse-fallback-backoff at 2026-03-02T01:17:04Z :rocket:

maya: Great, closing loop here. Please ping if the canary shows any regressions.

kevin: PR merged and rolled to canary. Will monitor metrics and post results tomorrow.

lina: Canary looks good so far — reconnect rate down 82% in window. :tada:
